data.title: Rapid Authorized User Addition Across Multiple Accounts
data.description: Detects the same individual being added as an authorized user across 3 or more credit accounts within 30 days. This technique is used in first-party bust-out and synthetic identity schemes to rapidly build credit history or gain access to multiple credit lines for coordinated bust-out. Authorized user tradelines inherit the primary account's payment history, allowing fraudsters to artificially inflate credit scores in weeks rather than months. When combined with subsequent high utilization, this pattern is a strong leading indicator of coordinated bust-out activity. The "piggybacking" of authorized user status is a well-documented credit manipulation technique exploited by both first-party fraudsters and synthetic identity rings.

enrichment_required.source: Credit bureau score for the authorized user at time of addition
Declared relationship between primary holder and authorized user

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Rapid Authorized User Addition")`
`comment("Detects same individual added as authorized user on 3+ accounts in 30 days")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:credit_monitoring
  event_type="authorized_user_added"
  earliest=-30d@d latest=now
| stats dc(account_id) as distinct_account_count,
        values(account_id) as accounts,
        values(primary_account_holder_id) as primary_holders,
        min(event_date) as first_addition,
        max(event_date) as last_addition
  by authorized_user_id, authorized_user_name
| where distinct_account_count >= 3
| eval addition_span_days = round((strptime(last_addition, "%Y-%m-%d") - strptime(first_addition, "%Y-%m-%d")) / 86400, 0)
| eval risk_score = case(
    distinct_account_count >= 5, "critical",
    distinct_account_count >= 4, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table authorized_user_id, authorized_user_name, distinct_account_count,
        accounts, primary_holders, first_addition, last_addition,
        addition_span_days, risk_score
| sort - distinct_account_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Rapid Authorized User Addition
-- Detects same individual added as authorized user on 3+ accounts in 30 days
SELECT
  au.authorized_user_id,
  au.authorized_user_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT au.account_id) AS distinct_account_count,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT au.account_id, ', ') AS accounts,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT au.primary_account_holder_id, ', ') AS primary_holders,
  MIN(au.event_date) AS first_addition,
  MAX(au.event_date) AS last_addition,
  DATEDIFF(DAY, MIN(au.event_date), MAX(au.event_date)) AS addition_span_days
FROM authorized_user_events au
WHERE au.event_type = 'authorized_user_added'
  AND au.event_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY au.authorized_user_id, au.authorized_user_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT au.account_id) >= 3
ORDER BY distinct_account_count DESC

references: LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Global State of Fraud and Identity Report (2026)
Federal Reserve, Synthetic Identity Fraud in the U.S. Payment System (2024)
CFPB, Authorized User Tradeline Abuse Advisory (2024)
falsepositives: Legitimate family financial management (parent adding child to multiple accounts)
Business owners adding trusted employees across corporate credit accounts
Credit repair services using authorized user tradeline strategies (legal but monitored)
